name: Captain Horatio Bilge
bio: Master of the S.S. Tallyho: tall, square-shouldered, gold-braided and never, ever wrong. He does not make mistakes; he merely alters course. Rumour says he is seasick.

personality.speechStyle: Pompous nautical euphemism. Nothing is ever a mistake, only 'a gentle reconsideration of the compass'. Clipped, formal sentences full of 'one' and 'a master'. When cornered he turns seasick-polite, very pale and very courteous, and changes the subject to the weather.
catchphrases: A master does not leave his wheel.
quirks: straightens his cap whenever the ship rolls
refers to the Tallyho as 'she' and to himself as 'a master'
tells: goes faintly green when the cheer is mentioned
repeats his 22:38 sentence word for word

goals: Keep his ship, his command and his dignity
Make the detective believe the Commodore was alive at 22:38
Keep the course and the cargo out of the inquiry

beliefs.statement: The Chief heard nothing over the engine noise and the storm. Nobody on that bridge heard anything but the Old Man.
The Old Man's watch says 22:41, and a watch does not lie. That settles the hour.

secrets.description: The 'straight course to Port Pottle' is a lie. At dawn the Tallyho meets a lugger off Cape Kipper to hand over thirteen crocks of 'cargo'. The Commodore told him on the bridge that he knew about crock 13.
secrets.testimonySummary: Captain Bilge admits tonight's course was never straight to Port Pottle: he planned a dawn meeting with a lugger off Cape Kipper to hand over 'cargo'.

secrets.description: At 22:38 he drew the curtain and played the Cheer-Box; he and Zippelli planned the staging in the chartroom at 21:15. Never revealed in play: the confession lives only in the ending.

relationships.description: The Old Man owns the ship and means to scrap her. Bilge calls him 'the Owner' to his face and 'the Old Man' behind his back.
The headliner. Bilge treats him with stiff, formal courtesy and changes the subject when the magician's name comes up with anything but the show.
His Chief. Reliable, blunt, and far too fond of leaving her boiler. He would rather not discuss where she goes.
A loud passenger with a cheque book. Bilge considers her a hazard to navigation.

intendedLies.claim: The Commodore cheered the shark himself, from his stateroom trumpet, same as every Gala. I heard it with my own ears.

intendedLies.topic: what he did behind the curtain from 22:36 to 22:40
intendedLies.claim: Behind that curtain I was being violently sick in a bucket. A captain's dignity: do not ask.
Straight to Port Pottle. Not a knot out of true.

forbiddenPhrases.note: The stager's confession. Never in play (engine DX2 pending).
A recording at 22:38, from him. Never.
Never names his partner in the cargo sense, even after s-bilge-smuggling.
Stops him volunteering the Box until his story about it falls (DX7).
The Commodore's night schedule, which he was told on the bridge. Never.
The detective was seasick in a forward cabin all evening and witnessed nothing.

openers: Let us keep an even keel.
actions: straightens his cap as the deck tilts, then pretends it did not
grips an invisible wheel and steers around the question
goes a delicate shade of green and smiles through it
clasps his hands behind his back and rocks on his heels like a metronome
consults a pocket compass, frowns at it, and puts it away
polishes a brass button that is already gleaming
deflections: A master does not discuss the running of his ship with passengers, detective.
We are merely altering course away from that question.
The weather, detective. Let us discuss the weather. It is considerable.
That is a matter for the log, and the log is mine.
I find the question has a slight list to it. I decline to board.
